news.title: AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns
news.why: Credit investors worry Jensen Huang's return means more circular financing: NVIDIA funding the customers that buy its chips.

news.title: CoreWeave bonds hit record lows, wiping out the Nvidia-driven rally
news.why: Bond buyers gave back Monday's jump in a day, a sign CoreWeave's credit still rests on NVIDIA's support rather than its own cash flow.

news.title: Nvidia's $30 billion OpenAI stake comes with up to $105 billion of lease guarantees
news.why: The guarantee is far bigger than the stake: if OpenAI can't pay rent on its Ohio campus, NVIDIA could owe it.

news.title: The data center financing gap: five-year servers, 30-year buildings
news.why: Chips wear out in about five years but the leases and loans run for decades, so lenders are betting on customers that may not last that long.

news.t: NVIDIA backs up to $105B of lease guarantees for an OpenAI data-center campus in Ohio, on top of a $30B equity stake.

Said customer loan guarantees take effect only once a project has financing and Nvidia gear is installed; its largest is a $105B backstop for OpenAI's Ohio campus (reports say cut from $250B). Shares fell 3.3% to $145.98 on Nov 19.
Fell 9.4% to $96.92 on Nov 19, the worst of the AI cloud names, as the Anthropic IPO failed to lift AI stocks.
Shares fell 16.8% to $128.64 after Nebius trimmed 2026 revenue to the low end of $3.0-3.4B; Q3 revenue rose 571% to $980.8M. Customer prepayments now cover 100% of new build costs.
Oracle rose about 11–12% on Nov 23 after NVIDIA brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, then fell about 4% on Nov 24.

Banks are selling Oracle-linked data-center construction loans at a discount: HSBC sold $300M of Project Jupiter debt below 90 cents after Oracle's force majeure notice, and ING is offering more in the mid-80s; shares fell 5.0% to $119.09 on Nov 16.
Anthropic's IPO filing shows at least $45B of computing commitments to Microsoft; shares fell 1.8% to $498.30 on Nov 19.
Owns nearly 10% of Anthropic (1.79B shares, about $149B at $83); Anthropic's Google commitments run up to $114.5B. Shares fell 3.5% to $272.66 on Nov 19.
Alphabet and Amazon together will own about 28% of Anthropic after its IPO, which is expected to price above its $70-78 range.
Fell 7.7% to $489.19 on Nov 19 after a short-seller report.
Fell 5.6% to $504.28 on Nov 16 after new US export limits on advanced AI chips to Southeast Asian countries.
Named by the ECB among eight firms holding over $4 trillion of AI commitments, mostly off their balance sheets, and said hyperscaler bond spreads are wider than similarly rated companies.
Downgraded to Neutral with the price target cut to $398 from $595; shares fell 4.8% to $347.01.
CoreWeave shares fell about 14% on Nov 24 and its 2031 and 2032 bonds hit record lows, erasing Monday's rally on Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA.
Fell 6.1% to $44.91 on Nov 19 as AI stocks slid despite Anthropic's debut.
Completed a €9B euro bond in six parts paying 4.3%-6.4% out to 2065; with $15B of dollar bonds and $37.5B of stock it raised about $62.6B in under a month. Long-term debt was $80.9B at Sep 30.
Morgan Stanley projects negative free cash flow of $2.8B in 2026, $10.4B in 2027 and $17.7B in 2028, and sees 2027 operating profit of $2.5B versus a $5.1B consensus.
Owns nearly 11% of Anthropic (1.92B shares, about $159B at the $83 IPO price); Anthropic has about $110B of commitments to Amazon.
Selling a 75% stake in 13 new data-center buildings to Blackstone's data-center REIT for $5B; AWS leases back 100% for 12 years (extendable to 32) and guarantees the rent.
A 13F filing showed Nvidia sold about 53.7M Intel shares in Q3, cutting its stake about 25% to roughly 161M shares; the stock sits about 62% below its $142.35 high.
Fell about 7% on Nov 16 with chip stocks; a shareholder lawsuit filed Nov 13 says Intel was slow to disclose weak PC sales and excess inventory before its nearly 29% one-day drop after Q3 results.
Agreed to buy private biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B, including milestone payments, so not all of it is paid upfront.

Q3 revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8B and it raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $2.84-2.89; total debt $64.3B after issuing $6.5B of long-term debt in the quarter, and nine-month free cash flow fell $2.0B to $6.8B.

SMCI.name: Super Micro Computer
SMCI.story: Sales almost quadrupled to $19.9B in the September quarter, but the business still burns cash: operations used $434M that quarter and about $7B over fiscal 2026, so growth is being funded with debt and convertible notes. One data-center customer was 44% of revenue.
issues: A single large data-center customer accounted for 44% of Q1 FY27 revenue; if it slows orders, revenue and the cash tied up in inventory move together.
Net income was $1.59B in Q1 FY27, yet operations used $434M of cash; fiscal 2026 free cash flow was about −$7B as inventory and receivables ballooned.
$8.6B of bank debt and convertible notes against $6.9B of cash leaves net debt of $1.7B.
Gross margin fell to 12.7% from 17.5% the quarter before, so small price or cost changes swing profit.

cm.label: Orders from its largest data-center customer (44% of sales)

val.why: Server makers trade at low multiples (Dell about 20x trailing earnings, Super Micro about 6x on Nov 13); 10x forward reflects thin margins, cash burn and one customer making up 44% of sales.

PLTR.name: Palantir Technologies
PLTR.story: A cash-rich software company with almost no debt: $10.4B of cash and Treasuries, revenue up 96% a year, and a 49% net margin in Q3 2026. The credit risk is low; the risk is in the share price, which already prices in years of fast growth.
issues: $10.4B of cash and Treasuries and essentially no borrowings.
The stock trades at a very high multiple of earnings, so a growth slowdown hits the price far more than the credit.
US commercial revenue just passed US government revenue for the first time; government budgets remain a swing factor.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Palantir has traded at roughly 60-150x forward adjusted earnings, far above software peers at 20-40x; 70x credits its fast growth but assumes some of the premium fades. Adjusted EPS is used because heavy stock pay lowers GAAP earnings.

MU.name: Micron Technology
MU.story: AI memory demand turned Micron into a cash machine: fiscal 2026 revenue of $133B, an 87% gross margin last quarter, and $68B of net cash. The risk is the memory cycle: prices that rose this fast can fall fast, while capex is climbing to build plants that open in 2027–2030.
issues: $5.2B of debt against $73.5B of cash and investments; two rating upgrades to BBB+ in the quarter.
Customers prepaid about $12.7B to lock in supply. It's cash today, but it's owed back as product, and it signals how tight the market is.
Capex climbing into a cyclical business
About $25B of capex planned for the first half of fiscal 2027 alone, more in the second half, for plants opening 2027–2030.

val.why: Memory makers trade at low multiples at the top of the cycle (Micron and SK Hynix have ranged about 5-12x forward earnings); 7x allows for profits falling once the memory shortage eases.

TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)
TSM.story: TSMC makes nearly every advanced AI chip and is one of the strongest credits in tech: about $126B of cash against $26B of debt, and a 58.7% operating margin in Q3 2026. Its risks are concentration in a few AI chip customers and geography, not its balance sheet.
issues: Roughly $126B of cash against $25.7B of debt; interest is covered more than 300 times by operating profit.
Q3 revenue rose 41% to $46.7B on AI demand; if Nvidia, AMD or Broadcom orders slow, TSMC feels it next.
About $50B of capex over the last year, funded entirely from roughly $95B of operating cash flow.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E (analyst consensus, per ADR), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: TSMC has traded at about 15-25x forward earnings, often below US chip designers because of Taiwan risk; 22x reflects its dominant share of AI chip production.

ARM.name: Arm Holdings
ARM.story: Arm licenses chip designs and carries almost no debt: $3.6B of cash against about $0.5B of debt. Revenue grew 27% to $1.44B last quarter, but royalties grew only 8% and cash from operations fell to $207M from $567M a year earlier.
issues: $3.62B of cash and short-term investments against about $0.5B of debt.
Royalty revenue rose just 8% to $670M, the slowest in eight quarters, while license revenue jumped 50% to $773M.
Operating cash flow fell to $207M from $567M and free cash flow to $110M from $411M a year earlier; GAAP operating margin was 13.9%.
SoftBank Group is the controlling shareholder, so decisions can reflect its funding needs.
sources: Arm Q2 FY27 shareholder letter (Arm Newsroom)

val.why: Arm has traded far above chip peers (over 200x trailing earnings) because investors pay for its royalty model; 60x forward still prices strong growth but allows for royalties growing only 8% last quarter.

ANET.name: Arista Networks
ANET.story: Arista has no debt and $14.4B of cash and securities, and revenue rose 58.5% to $3.66B in Q3 2026 with a 44.9% operating margin. The main risk is that a few cloud giants buy a large share of its gear.
issues: $2.3B of cash plus $12.1B of marketable securities and no borrowings.
Arista warns that a limited number of customers make up a substantial part of revenue; a pause by one cloud giant would show quickly.
Customers have paid or been billed $6.84B for products and services not yet recognized, which supports future revenue.

val.why: Fast-growing networking and AI hardware names have traded roughly 30-50x earnings (Arista about 53x trailing on Nov 13); 35x forward reflects 58% revenue growth but heavy reliance on a few cloud buyers.

VRT.name: Vertiv Holdings
VRT.story: Vertiv sells power and cooling gear for AI data centers; Q3 2026 sales rose 61% to $4.31B and orders more than doubled. It became investment grade in February 2026 and now holds slightly more cash ($3.7B) than debt ($3.4B).
issues: $3.71B of cash against $3.36B of debt after refinancing its secured loan with $2.1B of investment-grade bonds in March 2026.
Free cash flow of $652M in Q3 and about $3.15B over the last year; 2026 guidance raised to $2.6-2.8B.
Orders more than doubled on AI demand; if hyperscalers cut capex, Vertiv's orders would fall with them.

val.why: Vertiv traded near 38x trailing earnings on Nov 13 and power-equipment peers like Eaton and GE Vernova trade roughly 21-35x forward earnings; 30x credits orders that more than doubled but allows for a slowdown if data-center building cools.

CEG.name: Constellation Energy
CEG.story: The largest US nuclear operator took on debt to buy Calpine in January 2026 and now carries about $22-24B of net debt against about $8B of EBITDA. Long power contracts with Google and Amazon support the credit, and Q3 adjusted earnings rose 66% per share.
issues: About $24.7B of debt and $0.7B of cash; net debt was about $22.4B at Sep 30 per a third-party summary.
20-year deal with Google funding about $4.3B of nuclear uprates (890 MW) and a 20-year, 690 MW deal with Amazon at Calvert Cliffs.
Operating cash flow of about $4.2B was nearly all spent on $3.9B of capex over the last reported year, while buybacks reached $3.0B year to date.

val.why: Power producers with data-center contracts have traded at roughly 15-25x earnings (Vistra about 18x, Constellation about 22x trailing); 21x reflects Constellation's long nuclear contracts with Google and Amazon but also the extra debt from Calpine.

VST.name: Vistra
VST.rating: BBB- (S&P, raised to investment grade Dec 2025) / BBB- (Fitch)
VST.story: Vistra runs a large fleet of gas and nuclear plants and earns about $7.1-7.5B of adjusted EBITDA this year against roughly $20B of debt, close to 3x. It keeps borrowing to buy plants (Cogentrix for about $2.2B in October) and buy back stock, and Texas power policy is now the main swing factor.
issues: Issued about $8.0B of debt and repaid $3.9B in the first nine months of 2026; the $2.2B Cogentrix deal (5,500 MW of gas plants) closed in October, cutting liquidity from $8.9B to about $5.4B pro forma.
2026 adjusted EBITDA guided to $7.1-7.5B and 2027 to $7.7-8.5B, with free cash flow of $4.3-5.1B before growth spending.
Board added $1.5B of buyback authorization (about $2.5B left through 2028); $917M repurchased this year.

val.why: Power producers tied to data-center demand, like Constellation and Talen, have traded at roughly 15-25x forward earnings; 17x sits at the lower middle because Vistra carries more gas and Texas exposure.

sources: Vistra achieves investment-grade ratings from S&P and Fitch

MRVL.name: Marvell Technology
MRVL.sector: Custom AI chips and data-center networking
MRVL.story: Marvell designs custom AI chips and networking parts for the big cloud companies, so its growth rides on their spending plans. Debt of about $5.3B is small next to $3.9B of cash and $2.2B of yearly operating cash flow, and both rating agencies have upgraded it.
issues: Depends on a few cloud buyers

Data-center revenue grew 46% last quarter and management expects its custom-chip business to speed up sharply from the second half of FY2027, which ties results closely to a handful of cloud customers.
Long-term debt of $4.96B against $3.93B of cash at Aug 1, 2026; short-term debt was paid down to zero.
Spent $1.27B on acquisitions in the first half and issued $2.0B of convertible preferred stock in March 2026.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 6, 2026
val.why: AI chip designers such as Broadcom and Arm have traded at roughly 25-45x forward adjusted earnings; 30x reflects fast growth but heavy reliance on a few customers. Adjusted EPS is used because acquisition write-offs make GAAP P/E look much higher.

sources: S&P Global: credit divergence of Akamai and Marvell

QCOM.name: Qualcomm
QCOM.sector: Phone, car and data-center chips; patent licensing
QCOM.story: Qualcomm earns far more cash than it needs to cover about $15B of debt, but it is losing Apple's modem business and phone-chip sales fell 26% last quarter. It is pushing into cars and data centers, including a deal that can give an Amazon affiliate shares tied to up to $60B of purchases.
issues: Qualcomm expects Apple to mainly use its own modems going forward; handset chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14B in the September quarter and the December guide includes no Apple sales.
FY2026 operating cash flow about $11.2B versus total debt of $15.1B; it returned $11.7B through buybacks and dividends.
New bets on cars and data centers
Automotive revenue rose 52% to $6.0B in FY2026; it targets $5B of data-center sales in FY2027.

cm.label: Amazon affiliate warrant for up to 25M shares at $161.26, earned through purchases of up to $60B (term not disclosed)

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Qualcomm has traded at roughly 12-18x forward adjusted earnings, below faster-growing chip peers; 14x reflects the Apple loss offset by car and data-center growth. Adjusted EPS ($10.54 in FY2026) is used because GAAP EPS was lifted by a $5.7B tax benefit.

ASML.name: ASML Holding
ASML.story: ASML is the only maker of the most advanced chipmaking machines and holds far more cash ($14.5B) than debt ($2.2B). Its risk is demand, not borrowing: sales depend on chipmakers like TSMC continuing to expand for AI.
issues: Q3 sales hit a record €11.7B with a 57.5% gross margin; ASML says its 2027-28 supply will not fully meet customer demand.
About $14.5B of cash versus $2.2B of debt; euro bonds of €750M or less mature between 2027 and 2032.
2026 sales guided to €44-45B; a slowdown in AI-driven factory building would hit orders, and its China outlook is dimming.

val.why: ASML has usually traded at about 25-40x forward earnings, above equipment peers like Applied Materials and Lam (roughly 18-28x), because it has no competitor in advanced lithography; 30x is near the middle of its own range.

sources: ASML record Q3 2026 sales (Let's Data Science)
ASML capital return and financing (ratings, bonds)
ASML Q3 bookings and China outlook (Yahoo Finance)

CRM.name: Salesforce
CRM.rating: A (S&P, cut from A+ Nov 2026, stable) / A2 (Moody's)
CRM.story: Salesforce borrowed $25B in March to buy back its own stock, lifting total debt to about $42B, and S&P cut its rating one notch to A. It still makes about $15B a year of free cash flow, so the debt is manageable, but less cash is left for growth.
issues: Sold $25B of bonds to fund a $25B accelerated share buyback, cutting share count 10%; FY2027 free cash flow growth guidance was halved to 4-5%.
S&P lowered Salesforce to A from A+ on Nov 4, 2026, citing deals and the buyback; Moody's rates it A2.
Trailing operating cash flow about $15.8B and capex only $0.6B against $42.4B of debt.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Large software companies like Oracle, Adobe and ServiceNow have traded at roughly 15-35x forward adjusted earnings; Salesforce has sat near the low end as growth slowed, so 17x. Adjusted EPS is used because stock pay and deal costs depress GAAP earnings.

NOW.name: ServiceNow
NOW.story: ServiceNow spent $9.2B on acquisitions this year, mainly the $7.75B Armis purchase, and refinanced the bridge loan with a $4B bond that drew $38B of orders, so debt is about $7.5B against $7.0B of cash. It turns over $5B a year into operating cash and has $29.7B of contracted future revenue, so the credit picture is strong.
issues: $9.17B of acquisitions year to date, led by the $7.75B Armis deal; a $4B five-part bond in May 2026 replaced the bridge loan.
Q3 GAAP operating margin was 9.5% versus 32.5% adjusted, the gap mostly stock-based pay.
Q3 revenue rose 20.5% to $4.11B; remaining contracted revenue $29.7B (+22%); 2026 free cash flow margin target raised to 36%.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E of 22.46 at $101.97 (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 6, 2026
val.why: Large software peers in this dataset value at about 9-22x forward adjusted earnings (Adobe about 9x, Salesforce 17x fair value); ServiceNow grows about 20% a year, faster than either, so 24x. Adjusted EPS is used because stock pay depresses GAAP earnings.

ADBE.name: Adobe
ADBE.story: Adobe has about $6.4B of debt against $5.6B of cash and makes over $10B a year of operating cash, so debt is small. The main risk is to the business, not the balance sheet: investors worry AI tools will undercut its subscriptions, and it is spending heavily on buybacks ($2.2B last quarter) during a CEO transition.
issues: The stock trades near 9x forward earnings on fears AI image and video tools erode its subscriptions, though AI-first annual recurring revenue grew more than 150%.
The Q3 release signals a CEO handover from Shantanu Narayen; Steve Day is interim CFO.
Bought back about 9.5M shares for $2.23B in Q3 while repaying $250M of debt; remaining contracted revenue $22.16B.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E of 8.91 at $239.30 (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 6, 2026
val.why: Mature software firms in this dataset are valued at about 14-24x forward adjusted earnings (Salesforce 17x); Adobe's growth is slowing to about 10% and AI threatens its core, so 14x at the low end. Adjusted EPS is used because amortization and stock pay lower GAAP EPS.

SNOW.name: Snowflake
SNOW.story: Snowflake still loses money on a GAAP basis (about $1.1B over the last year, mostly stock-based pay) but generates about $1.2B of free cash flow and holds $4.3B of cash against $2.8B of mostly convertible debt. Revenue is growing about 35% with $9B of contracted future revenue, so near-term credit risk is low.
issues: Trailing net loss about $1.09B; Q2 GAAP operating loss $263M versus $237M adjusted operating profit.
$4.34B of cash and investments against $2.76B of debt; trailing free cash flow about $1.2B.
Q2 revenue up 35% to $1.55B; full-year product revenue guidance raised to $6.07B; next results Dec 2, 2026.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E of 115.37 at $291 (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Snowflake has no GAAP profit and negative EBITDA, so adjusted EPS is used; fast-growing data software peers like Palantir and Datadog have traded at very high multiples, and 80x forward credits ~35-40% growth while sitting below today's 115x.

IREN.name: IREN
IREN.sector: AI cloud / data centers (former bitcoin miner)
IREN.story: IREN is turning from a bitcoin miner into an AI cloud provider with a $20.3B contract backlog led by Microsoft, but its debt rose to $10.2B (net debt $4.4B, up from $0.2B a quarter earlier). It still needs about $6B of its $15B planned spending this fiscal year from financing not yet secured, and its revenue ramp has slipped to early 2027.
issues: Of about $15B of remaining FY27 capex, $9B is covered by cash, GPU financing and prepayments; the other $6B depends on new financing.
Total debt $10.21B at Sep 30 vs $7.84B in June; net debt $4.43B vs $0.22B; drew $2.36B from a financing facility in the quarter.
Target of over $4B annualized AI revenue moved from end-2026 to January (possibly February) 2027; Q1 revenue $228M, net loss $263M.
Fell 9.8% to $16.39 on Nov 16, a 52-week low (high $70.71), making new share sales costlier.

cm.label: Multi-year Microsoft AI cloud contract, partly prepaid
Remaining FY27 data-center and GPU spending plan

val.why: IREN has GAAP losses and slightly negative trailing EBITDA, so earnings-based values don't work yet (quarterly adjusted EBITDA was $66M); AI-cloud peers like CoreWeave and Nebius have traded around 10-20x forward EBITDA, so 15x, but the fair value only becomes meaningful once EBITDA turns positive.

sources: IREN delays $4B target, seeks $6B (Let's Data Science)

WULF.name: TeraWulf
WULF.rating: BB (S&P) / Ba2 (Moody's) / BB (Fitch) on the $3.2B Wulf Compute secured notes; parent not rated
WULF.story: TeraWulf has signed long leases worth about $25.7B, including a 20-year, roughly $19B deal with Anthropic, with Google providing credit support, but today it earns only about $76M a quarter and burns cash building sites. Debt is about $5.2B ($3.2B of 7.75% secured notes plus convertibles) against $1.6B of unrestricted cash.
issues: Nine-month operating cash flow -$178.9M and capex $2.23B; trailing free cash flow about -$3.35B.
Q3 net income of $709.9M came from a $728.4M non-cash warrant gain; adjusted EBITDA was -$12.8M.
$3.2B of 7.75% secured notes due 2030 plus about $2.1B of convertible notes; revolver raised to $400M.
Anthropic 20-year lease (~401 MW, ~$19B) backed by a Google credit backstop; Fluidstack leases at Lake Mariner.

cm.label: Anthropic 20-year data-center lease at Justified, Kentucky (~401 MW), Google-backed financing
Fluidstack 10-year leases at Lake Mariner, Google credit support

val.why: TeraWulf has negative EBITDA today, so a fair value can't be computed from earnings yet; data-center landlords with long leases have traded around 15-25x EBITDA, and 15x sits at the low end for a company still building most of its capacity.

GEV.name: GE Vernova
GEV.sector: Gas turbines, grid equipment and wind
GEV.rating: BBB- (S&P, outlook positive, last action found May 2025) / BBB (Fitch, outlook positive)
GEV.story: GE Vernova sells the gas turbines and grid gear that power new data centers; it holds $16.8B of cash against about $2.8B of borrowings and a record $197B backlog. The main credit change ahead is its roughly €8B Trench purchase, to be paid half in cash and half with new debt.
issues: $16.8B of cash against $2.83B of borrowings and finance leases; a $6B credit line is undrawn.
Q3 orders were $29.3B, up 96% organic; gas turbine backlog plus reservations reached 122 GW.
Agreed to buy Trench Group for about €8B ($9.0B), funded about equally with cash and debt, closing late 2027.

Trailing net income of $10.4B is far above Q3's $1.3B, likely helped by revaluing its old 50% Prolec GE stake when it bought the rest for about $5.2B, so the ~20x trailing P/E looks cheaper than it is.
Nine-month operating cash flow of $16.7B; 2026 free cash flow guidance raised to $16-17B, and $9.9B of shares bought back since Dec 2024.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E of 34.56 at $803.13 (analyst consensus), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: GE Vernova trades near 35x forward earnings while Eaton is about 21x and Vertiv about 38x trailing; 30x credits its record backlog but allows for slower orders. Forward EPS is used because the trailing figure includes a one-time accounting gain.

sources: S&P outlook to positive, BBB- affirmed (May 2025)

ETN.name: Eaton
ETN.sector: Electrical equipment for data centers and grids
ETN.story: Eaton makes switchgear, power distribution and cooling gear that data centers need; Q3 2026 sales rose 28% to $8.9B and its electrical backlog is up 46%. Debt rose to about $20B after buying Boyd Thermal for $9.55B, but steady cash flow keeps it solidly investment grade.
issues: About $20.1B of debt (including $1.6B short-term) against $0.8B of cash and short-term investments after the $9.55B Boyd Thermal and $1.53B Ultra PCS deals.
Electrical backlog up 46% from a year earlier (about $20.4B); rolling orders up 39% in the Americas and 51% globally.
Q3 free cash flow of $1.03B; trailing operating cash flow about $4.9B against $1.1B of capex.
Much of the order surge comes from data centers; a pullback in AI capex would slow orders.

val.src: StockAnalysis forward P/E of 21.37 at $341.72 (analyst consensus, adjusted EPS), Nov 6, 2026
val.why: Power-equipment peers trade from about 21x (Eaton today) to 35x (GE Vernova) forward earnings; 24x credits strong data-center demand at a modest premium to today. Adjusted EPS is used because acquisition amortization lowers GAAP earnings (2026 guidance: $13.70-13.80 adjusted vs $10.39-10.49 GAAP).

sources: S&P A- on Eaton Capital notes

CIFR.name: Cipher Digital
CIFR.story: Cipher has signed long data-center leases, including a 20-year Barber Lake lease with a leading AI lab worth about $9.1B and a 15-year AWS lease, but today it earns only about $27M a quarter. It has borrowed about $5.6B, mostly 6.1-7.1% secured notes, to build the sites.
issues: Trailing operating cash flow about -$338M and capex about $2.75B, so free cash flow is about -$3.1B.
About $5.6B of debt ($3.73B of secured notes at 6.125-7.125% plus $850M of 0% convertibles due 2032) against trailing revenue of $146M.
Q3 net income of $31.6M came despite an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $10M; nine-month net loss was $350.2M.
Barber Lake lease extended to 20 years (about $9.1B total) with a leading AI lab; 300 MW, 15-year lease with AWS at Black Pearl, where rent began in Q3.

cm.label: Barber Lake 20-year lease with a leading AI lab
AWS 15-year, 300 MW lease at Black Pearl

val.why: Cipher has almost no EBITDA yet, so a fair value can't be computed from earnings; data-center landlords with long leases have traded around 15-25x EBITDA, and 15x sits at the low end for a company still building most of its capacity.

sources: Cipher Digital Q3 2026 results (Finviz / press release)
Cipher Q3 2026 revenue and balance sheet (Webull)
Cipher $3.73B secured notes, AWS and Google leases (Rallies)

APLD.name: Applied Digital
APLD.rating: Not rated at parent level; data-center debt is privately placed secured notes
APLD.story: Applied Digital has leased about 1.4 GW of data-center capacity to CoreWeave and investment-grade cloud giants, worth about $36B over the base terms, but it is building well ahead of the rent: trailing capex of about $4.7B dwarfs $0.87B of revenue. Debt is about $6.4B, mostly project-level secured notes at 7-9.25%, against about $2.9B of cash.
issues: Trailing capex about $4.69B against operating cash flow of $0.24B, so free cash flow is about -$4.5B.
Total debt $6.38B, including $2.35B of 9.25% notes due 2030 and $1.59B of 7.0% notes due 2031; interest expense was $77.4M last quarter.
Q1 FY27 net loss of $184.1M; adjusted EBITDA of +$64.4M on revenue of $341.9M, of which $183.5M was one-time tenant fit-out work.
About 1.41 GW leased across five campuses with ~$36B of base-term contracted revenue, including a 210 MW, 15-year, ~$5.2B hyperscaler lease at Delta Forge 2.

cm.label: CoreWeave 15-year leases at Polaris Forge 1, North Dakota (~400 MW)
Investment-grade hyperscaler 15-year lease at Delta Forge 2, Alabama (210 MW)

sources: Applied Digital finalizes 150 MW CoreWeave expansion (StreetInsider)

CORZ.name: Core Scientific
CORZ.story: Core Scientific has turned its bitcoin sites into AI data centers leased mainly to CoreWeave (about 590 MW, $10B+ over 12 years) and to AMD and an AMD-backed cloud (about 530 MW), for more than $24B of contracted revenue. It borrowed heavily to build: long-term debt rose to $4.3B from $1.1B at the end of 2025, including $3.3B of secured notes repaid from CoreWeave's rent.
issues: Long-term debt $4.30B at Sep 30 vs $1.06B at Dec 31, 2025; cash fell to $804M from $1.77B in one quarter as quarterly capex hit $985M.
About 485 MW is billing, all of it CoreWeave, which itself carries about $47B of debt; the $3.3B of secured notes due 2031 are paid from a lockbox of CoreWeave rent.
Q3 net income of $1.18B came mainly from a $1.03B non-cash warrant gain; adjusted EBITDA was $133.6M on $232.9M of revenue.
CoreWeave leases run 12 years with two 5-year options, take-or-pay with annual escalators; the company says over half of contracted cash flow is backed by investment-grade credit.

cm.label: CoreWeave 12-year colocation leases (~590 MW across five sites)
AMD and AMD-backed cloud leases (~530 MW, deliveries 2027-28); value estimated as remainder of $24B+ total

val.why: Core Scientific's yearly EBITDA is still small while most leases ramp up, so earnings-based value is unreliable; data-center landlords with long leases have traded around 15-25x EBITDA, and 15x sits at the low end given its reliance on CoreWeave.

LRCX.name: Lam Research
LRCX.story: Lam makes the etch and deposition machines used to build memory and logic chips, and holds about $7.4B of cash against $3.7B of debt. Its risk is a slowdown in chipmaker spending and its dependence on China, which was 35% of sales last quarter.
issues: Cash of $7.44B vs total debt of $3.74B; trailing operating cash flow $7.58B against capex of about $1.0B.
China was 35% of September-quarter revenue, leaving Lam exposed to further US export limits.
September-quarter revenue $8.22B (vs $6.72B in June) at a 40% operating margin; December-quarter guidance $8.6B.
Bought back $1.02B of stock and paid $0.33B of dividends last quarter, well within $3.50B of operating cash flow.

val.src: Implied by StockAnalysis forward P/E of 21.98 at $225.92 (analyst consensus), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Chip-equipment makers like Applied Materials, KLA and Lam have traded at roughly 18-30x forward earnings; 24x sits mid-range, balancing strong AI memory demand against Lam's heavy China exposure.

sources: Lam Research results for quarter ended Sep 27, 2026 (SEC exhibit 99.1)

AMAT.name: Applied Materials
AMAT.story: Applied Materials is the largest maker of chipmaking machines; fiscal 2026 sales rose 21% to $34.4B and it holds about $14.1B of cash and investments against $6.5B of debt. Its risk is a slowdown in chipmaker spending, not its borrowing.
issues: Cash and investments of $14.10B vs total debt of $6.53B ($1.30B due within a year).
Q4 revenue $10.41B, up 53%; guided Q1 FY27 revenue of $11.1B and adjusted EPS of $4.35.
Fiscal 2026 buybacks of $3.18B and dividends of $1.57B, versus operating cash flow of $8.87B and capex of $2.67B.
Orders depend on chipmakers continuing to build AI-related factories; a pause would hit sales quickly.

val.src: Implied by StockAnalysis forward P/E of 19.31 at $370.50 (analyst consensus), Nov 13, 2026
val.why: Chip-equipment makers like Lam and KLA have traded at roughly 18-30x forward earnings; 22x sits in the lower half, reflecting Applied's larger size and more cyclical mix.

KLAC.name: KLA Corporation
KLAC.story: KLA makes the inspection and measurement tools chipmakers use to catch defects, and earns the highest margins in the equipment group. It carries about $6.0B of debt against $4.7B of cash, comfortably covered by $4.5B of yearly operating cash flow.
issues: Trailing operating cash flow $4.51B and free cash flow $4.04B; capital returns of $3.79B over the same 12 months.
September-quarter revenue $4.14B, up 29% from $3.21B a year earlier; December-quarter guidance $4.7B.
Long-term debt $5.72B vs cash and securities of $4.74B; $936M of buybacks last quarter keep cash from building.

val.why: KLA has usually traded at a premium to Applied Materials and Lam (which trade roughly 18-30x forward) because of its higher margins and steadier service revenue; 26x is in the upper half of that range.
